title: Monotonicity of Bounded Execution
statement: Let $\mathrm{Ends}(s,\sigma,T,Q)$ mean that statement $s$ has an execution from state $\sigma$ to some state satisfying $Q$, with cost at most $T$. For any limits, program, depth, statement, initial state, natural numbers $T,T'$, and state predicates $Q,Q'$, if $\mathrm{Ends}(s,\sigma,T,Q)$, $T\le T'$, and every state satisfying $Q$ also satisfies $Q'$, then $\mathrm{Ends}(s,\sigma,T',Q')$.
hypotheses_covered: An execution of the statement from the initial state ends in a state satisfying $Q$ with cost at most $T$
